syllabusTopics: Numerical computation: roots of algebraic and transcendental equations (bisection and Newton-Raphson method)
Numerical integration: Trapezoidal rule and Simpson's rule
Mechanics (optional): Statics — forces and resultant forces, parallelogram law of forces, composition and resolution of forces, resultant of coplanar forces acting on a point
Mechanics (optional): Dynamics — motion of particle in a straight line, motion with uniform acceleration, motion under gravity, motion down a smooth inclined plane

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Unsolvable-by-formula equations surrender to iteration: bisection halves a bracketing interval (slow, certain), Newton-Raphson slides down the tangent (fast, needs a good start): xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ). Numerical integration does the same for areas: trapezoidal averages heights into trapezoids, Simpson fits parabolas through triplets (needs even strips). The mechanics option mirrors physics: parallelogram of forces, inclined-plane motion.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Newton–Raphson: xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ)  ·  bisection: halve [a,b] keeping f(a)·f(b) < 0  ·  trapezoidal: h/2·[y₀ + 2Σyᵢ + yₙ]  ·  Simpson 1/3: h/3·[y₀ + 4Σodd + 2Σeven + yₙ] (n EVEN)  ·  forward-difference tables extrapolate from the top (NEB 2022 MCQ)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Newton needs f′ ≠ 0 near the root and a close x₀ — bad starts cycle or flee. Bisection needs a sign change on [a,b] (continuity assumed). Simpson demands an EVEN number of strips; trapezoidal accepts any n. Forward differences assume EQUAL x-intervals.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: x³ − 2x − 5 = 0 from x₀ = 2: f = −1, f′ = 3x²−2 = 10 → x₁ = 2.1; iterate to 2.0946 (three decimals, NEB 2023). Multiple roots slow Newton to linear crawl. Simpson beats trapezoidal on smooth curves (exact for cubics); rough data favours trapezoidal's humility.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: x³ − 2x − 5 = 0, x₀ = 2: f(2) = −1, f′(x) = 3x² − 2 → f′(2) = 10 → x₁ = 2 − (−1)/10 = 2.1. Next: f(2.1) = 0.061, f′ = 11.23 → x₂ ≈ 2.0946; one more pass stabilises 2.095 (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Always show f, f′, and each iterate.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Newton can diverge, oscillate (x²+1 = 0 has no real root to find) or stall at stationary points. Bisection converges surely but slowly (one binary digit per step). Simpson on odd strips is undefined — miscounting n is the classic lost mark.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Newton from Taylor: f(x) ≈ f(xₙ) + f′(xₙ)(x−xₙ) = 0 → x = xₙ − f/f′ — each step solves the LINEARISATION, converging quadratically near simple roots (correct digits roughly double). Trapezoidal from piecewise-linear area; Simpson from integrating the parabola through each (x₀,x₁,x₂) triplet, giving the 1–4–2–4…–1 weights.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Root questions: write f, f′, x₀, then iterate in a table — examiners award step marks per row. 'Three decimal places' means iterate until the 3rd decimal freezes. Integration: even strips + smooth → Simpson; else trapezoidal. Forward differences → top-of-table extrapolation (NEB 2022 MCQ).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): x³ − 2x − 5 = 0 by Newton-Raphson from x₀ = 2 (3 d.p.). NEB 2022 (1): forward differences extrapolate from the table's beginning (MCQ). Bisection steps and trapezoidal/Simpson area numericals rotate yearly.
